newsitem.title: UK: Zinc breaks $1,400 on LME, highest since Oct'90.
newsitem.headline: Zinc breaks $1,400 on LME, highest since Oct'90.

text.p: Zinc prices broke above the $1,400 a tonne levels during Friday afternoon London Metal Exchange (LME) trading, to hit the highest for 6-3/4 year highs.
Traders said renewed speculative buying finally cleared the stubborn resistance around $1,400, with three months prices $8 higher at $1,401.
Zinc is being underpinned largely by technical buying and speculative interest at present, although there is an strong fundamental picture.
Inventory levels are falling on the LME, consistent with a market that is heading for a supply/demand deficit in 1997.
Stocks currently stand at 425,800 tonnes, down over 76,000 tonnes, or 15 percent, already this year.
But analysts cautioned the pace and extent of the move. There is little consumer interest at these high levels, while there is persistent talk of sizeable Chinese exports being shipped to Singapore.
